title: Payment Gateways in India: Security, Compliance and Data Protection
summary: Compare payment gateway security in India: PCI DSS, tokenisation, RBI compliance, data protection and merchant support, including Razorpay.
body_markdown:
Payment gateway security is the set of controls that protects payment data and transactions, including card-data handling, encryption, authentication and fraud monitoring. For an Indian merchant, the right comparison also covers PCI DSS responsibilities, RBI requirements, customer-data protection and the help available when a payment needs investigation.


This guide compares Razorpay with two anonymised alternatives, Payment Gateway A and Payment Gateway B. Start with the tables below, then use the detailed sections to check the controls, integration and support your business needs. Razorpay brings together documented checkout choices, TokenHQ, scoped risk tools, and Ray assistance; availability and responsibilities depend on your account and deployment.


A provider’s certification is evidence about an assessed service. Your business must still confirm its own validation requirements and protect the parts of the payment flow it controls.


## Key Takeaways


- **Razorpay documents PCI DSS Level 1 compliance.** Managed checkout can reduce merchant card-data handling, while merchants remain responsible for validating their own integration and systems.
- **TokenHQ supports saved-card tokenisation without merchants retaining raw card numbers.** Tokenisation protects saved credentials; hosted card entry limits exposure during collection.
- **Razorpay documents TLS encryption and field-level protection for personal information.** These controls complement tokenisation by protecting customer data beyond card numbers.
- **Razorpay provides KYC requirements by business type.** Merchants should also verify RBI authorisation for the contracting legal entity and payment activity.
- **Razorpay documents 3DS2 for international cards and risk tools for eligible Indian exporters.** Its Risk Analytics Dashboard exposes fraud-to-sales, dispute-to-sales and risk-decline metrics.
- **Ray provides WhatsApp-based payment assistance and supported account actions for eligible merchants.** Dashboard tickets and documented escalation routes support issues requiring further investigation.


## Razorpay vs Payment Gateway A vs Payment Gateway B: Security and Support Compared


Razorpay combines published security and shared-responsibility guidance with TokenHQ, scoped authentication and risk tools, and Ray merchant assistance. For a business comparing gateways, the practical benefit is a documented path from selecting the checkout to managing payment questions and escalation. Use the same criteria for all three providers and confirm the features available to your account.

Treat these as screening layers alongside authentication, fulfilment checks and your own fraud operations.[Risk monitoring](https://razorpay.com/docs/security/?preferred-country=IN) . Describes velocity limits and risk-based transaction controls. Confirm which controls and reports your merchant account can inspect or configure.


Evidence of better security outcomes Use the documented risk indicators to support your evaluation, then compare confirmed fraud loss, false declines and incidents on the same transaction mix. PCI DSS evidence and tokenisation appear across all three providers. Razorpay’s documented responsibility model helps you connect those controls to the integration your team will deploy. Its TokenHQ and product-specific authentication documentation also make the prerequisites explicit, so you can plan the right payment flow and evidence review.

### When Is Razorpay a Strong Fit?


Razorpay brings together a documented merchant-responsibility model, TokenHQ saved-card flows, product-specific authentication guidance and tracked operational support. For Indian exporters receiving international payments, its Risk Analytics Dashboard names the fraud-to-sales, dispute-to-sales and risk-decline indicators a team can monitor. For eligible accounts, Ray adds English/Hindi text and voice assistance on WhatsApp for payment questions and supported actions. These are concrete reasons to shortlist Razorpay when those workflows match your business. The alternatives also document substantial security and AI capabilities; suitability depends on the integration, account access and support terms you will actually use.


### Which Core Metrics Should You Compare?


Ask every provider for the same transaction mix and observation period: confirmed fraud loss in basis points of processed value; false declines as a share of assessed legitimate attempts; comparable reportable incidents; median and p90 first useful response and resolution times; and reopened-ticket rate. Test AI answer accuracy and authorised-action completion on the same tasks. Published capabilities alone do not establish those results, and this review does not supply a matched performance ranking.


## How Should You Compare Payment Gateways on Security and Compliance?


Compare payment gateways using current compliance evidence, the actual card-data path, supported tokenisation and authentication, merchant responsibilities, and operational help. Ask what each control covers, which account or integration can use it, and what remains your responsibility. A feature name alone is not enough to assess suitability.


### Security, Compliance and Data Protection Answer Different Questions


Security is about protecting systems and transactions: access control, monitoring, encryption and fraud screening. Compliance is about the obligations that apply to your entity and activity, and the evidence that demonstrates them. Data protection is about collecting, using, sharing, retaining and deleting information appropriately. A control can be good security practice without being a statutory mandate, and a compliance document does not by itself prove a control works in your deployment.


### Turn Feature Claims Into Evidence Requests


Three questions convert marketing copy into something you can file:


1. **Can you show the service scope?** Which legal entity was assessed, for which services, over which period.
2. **Where do card details travel?** In the exact integration you plan to deploy, not in a best-case architecture diagram.
3. **What happens when the workflow fails?** A failed payment, a refund that has not credited, a disputed transaction.


Use a three-part framework for the file you retain: evidence reviewed, integration verified, responsibilities recorded.


## How Can a PCI DSS-Compliant Gateway Reduce Merchant Compliance Burden?


Razorpay’s public security documentation lists PCI DSS Level 1. For a merchant, the potential reduction in card-data handling depends on the supported checkout flow and its implementation. Review the provider’s current service evidence, then confirm your own validation requirements. Provider compliance does not automatically certify your website or business.


The[Razorpay security documentation](https://razorpay.com/docs/security/?preferred-country=IN) describes the provider’s published status. The PCI Security Standards Council explains that[outsourcing payment processing does not remove every merchant obligation](https://www.pcisecuritystandards.org/faqs/does-pci-dss-apply-to-merchants-who-outsource-all-payment-processing-operations-and-never-store-process-or-transmit-cardholder-data/) . Request current evidence for the service and legal entity you will use.


### Provider Evidence Is Not a Merchant Certificate


An Attestation of Compliance records that a named entity was assessed for named services over a defined period. Your validation is a separate exercise, usually a self-assessment questionnaire or a report agreed with your acquiring bank, covering your website, systems and processes. Level 1 is a validation classification, rather than a different version of PCI DSS. Confirm the applicable classification and validation route with the relevant acquirer or payment brand.


### Match the Assessment to the Real Integration


Managed card entry can reduce the cardholder data your systems handle. The exact implementation still matters. The PCI Security Standards Council’s[SAQ A script-attack guidance](https://www.pcisecuritystandards.org/faqs/1588/) applies specifically to merchant webpages containing an embedded payment page or form. That particular eligibility criterion does not apply in the same way to redirect-only flows or fully outsourced payment links. Confirm all eligibility criteria for your deployment and review scripts that can affect payment security.


**DID YOU KNOW #1:** Outsourcing payment processing never removes every merchant obligation. The split is explained in our guide to[Razorpay Checkout and merchant PCI DSS responsibilities](https://razorpay.com/blog/pci-dss-compliant-payment-gateway-india/) .


## Tokenisation, Hosted Checkout and Hosted Fields: What Keeps Card Data Away From Your Servers?


Razorpay documents TokenHQ and managed checkout options for supported saved-card and payment flows. Tokenisation and card-entry isolation are separate design decisions. Before choosing an integration, trace where raw card details travel and confirm the exact supported option. Customising a checkout does not by itself prove that it uses isolated hosted fields.


### Distinguish Card Entry From Saved-Card Tokenisation


Card entry is about the moment the customer types a card number: which party’s code renders that field, and which party’s systems receive the value. Tokenisation is about what happens afterwards, when an eligible saved credential is reused. The two can be configured independently. A token also does not mean your systems hold nothing sensitive: order records, customer names, addresses and payment references still flow to you.


For saved cards, evaluate the supported token-requestor role and network flow rather than assuming that a tokenisation label describes every integration.

The S2S documentation is explicit that the merchant can capture payment details on its own server. That is the clearest case where your obligations increase rather than reduce.


### TokenHQ Supports Specific Roles and Prerequisites


[TokenHQ](https://razorpay.com/card-tokenisation/) covers the saved-card and network-token capability, including the distinction between Razorpay acting as token requestor and a business acting as its own token requestor. The[business-as-requestor flow](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/payment-methods/cards/token-hq/merchant-requestor-with-network-tokens/) is available on demand and for PCI-compliant merchants, so do not apply its prerequisites to every Standard Checkout saved-card feature. For the documented Razorpay-as-token-requestor flow, the[network activation notes](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/payment-methods/cards/token-hq/razorpay-requestor-with-network-tokens/additional-information/) specify different go-live timings. Confirm the current timing for your networks and account. If token portability matters, ask which token-requestor flow, network rules and integration prerequisites apply.


**DID YOU KNOW #2:** A token protects a particular payment credential or flow. It does not replace appropriate handling of names, addresses, order records or support attachments.


## How Do Encryption and Customer-Data Controls Complement Tokenisation?


Tokenisation replaces a payment credential with a substitute reference; encryption protects information in its applicable transmission or storage context. A merchant should also review access, logs, retention and support data. Evaluate these controls together, because reducing card storage does not remove the need to protect other customer information.


### Keep Encryption Claims Specific


Razorpay’s[security documentation](https://razorpay.com/docs/security/?preferred-country=IN) describes HTTPS using TLS and field-level encryption for personally identifiable information. These are specific controls you can assess alongside your own access and logging practices. Ask which services and data categories each control covers. A cipher or protocol name alone does not establish that one gateway produces better security outcomes.


### Review Customer Information Beyond Card Numbers


Ask who inside your business can view full order information, what customer data enters application logs, what gets pasted into support tickets, and which retention terms apply. Razorpay’s[published privacy policy](https://razorpay.com/privacy-policy/) describes its handling terms, though a policy is a statement of practice rather than an independent audit. The Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 have phased commencement. Map the provisions applicable to your business and service to your notice, retention and data-handling processes. Check incident reporting and contractual notification duties separately.


An illustrative scenario, not a recorded incident: a merchant removes all backend card collection, then a support agent attaches a screenshot of a full order record to a chat thread. The card data risk fell. The personal data risk did not. For technical depth, see our[card and customer-data tokenisation and encryption checklist](https://razorpay.com/blog/payment-gateway-tokenisation-encryption-india/) .


## What Should Indian Merchants Verify About RBI, KYC and AML Compliance?


Start with the legal entity and payment activity in your agreement, then check the applicable RBI authorisation and onboarding requirements. Review merchant KYC, settlement and grievance terms separately from technical security. A gateway’s authorisation does not transfer all of your business’s compliance duties.


The governing instrument is the RBI Master Direction on Regulation of Payment Aggregators, dated 15 September 2025. A payment aggregator receives funds from customers and settles them to merchants, which is why it carries onboarding, escrow and due-diligence duties. A payment gateway in the narrow technical sense routes transaction data. Consumer payment apps, banks and verification APIs are different services again.


### Match Entity, Activity and Contract


Request the contracting entity name, the relevant authorisation category, current evidence and the settlement terms. Then verify it against the RBI list of payment aggregator applications and authorisations rather than a vendor summary. Payment data storage obligations stem from RBI’s Storage of Payment System Data circular, which places responsibility on authorised payment system operators.


### Merchant Onboarding Is Different From Your Customer KYC


Razorpay publishes[KYC requirements by business type](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/business-types-kyc-documents/?preferred-country=IN) , showing that documentation depends on your constitution and activity. That is onboarding due diligence on you as a merchant. It is not proof that a provider offers a customer video-KYC or AML-screening API for your own users. The RBI PA directions also require ongoing monitoring against merchant business profiles and, for non-bank PAs, FIU-IND registration and applicable reporting. Ask how document re-review and unusual activity are handled. These provider duties do not replace any obligations that separately apply to your own business.


**PRO-TIP #2:** Ask what documents and consents are required, what can trigger a re-review, and where onboarding issues should be escalated. For the verification steps, use our guide to[verifying an RBI-authorised payment aggregator](https://razorpay.com/blog/how-to-verify-an-rbi-authorised-payment-aggregator-in-india/) .


## Which Authentication and Risk Controls Matter for Higher-Risk Transactions?


Assess authentication separately from fraud monitoring. Authentication helps verify the payer; monitoring helps assess transaction risk. Razorpay’s documented 3DS2 card feature is scoped to international cards, while its Risk Analytics Dashboard is described for Indian exporters. Confirm supported channels and account availability for the transactions you actually process.


### Domestic and International Card Flows Need Separate Answers


The RBI’s September 2025 authentication announcement describes additional issuer risk checks beyond minimum two-factor authentication and retains SMS OTP as an available factor. It gives 1 April 2026 as the general compliance date, subject to directions with a different date. Confirm the applicable transaction scope, exemptions and issuer responsibilities rather than applying one flow to every payment.


Keep that separate from 3DS2. Razorpay’s[3DS2 documentation](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/payment-methods/cards/features/3ds2.0/?preferred-country=IN) describes support for international card payments, with browser and app or SDK channels differing in availability. Do not convert that into a universal domestic-card capability, and do not import European SCA rules as India’s framework. Authentication success, payment success and fraud-loss outcomes measure three different things.


### Compare Monitoring, Rules and Investigation Tools


Ask each provider which suspicious-transaction signals exist, which rules you can configure, who reviews flagged transactions, and what dispute evidence the system retains. Razorpay’s[Risk Analytics Dashboard](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/international-payments/risk-visibility-dashboard/) is documented for Indian exporters receiving international payments, so do not assume it is enabled for every domestic account. An issuer-side authentication service is not evidence that you control that engine, and payment routing is a reliability feature, not an AML guarantee.


**DID YOU KNOW #3:** A successful authentication is not proof that a transaction is risk-free. Our[domestic and international authentication guide](https://razorpay.com/blog/strong-customer-authentication-payments-india/) sets out the scope differences.


## How Does Merchant Support Work From Onboarding to Escalation?


Evaluate support across the merchant lifecycle: onboarding, integration, payment investigation, refunds, settlements, disputes and unresolved issues. Razorpay documents technical help, Dashboard tickets and escalation, while Ray offers announced WhatsApp assistance for account queries and supported actions. Check availability, permissions and human contact separately from resolution quality.


### Start With Onboarding and Integration Help


Start onboarding by preparing the right documents. The[business-type KYC documentation](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/business-types-kyc-documents/?preferred-country=IN) tells you what to assemble before you apply. Technical and product queries route through the[documented support process](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/dashboard/support/?preferred-country=IN) . Keep two things apart: a developer troubleshooting a webhook signature is a support topic, while a compliance team’s approval of your business category is a review decision with its own timeline.


### Follow the Payment Through Refunds and Settlements


[Ray](https://razorpay.com/ray-on-whatsapp/) is presented as WhatsApp-based account assistance covering payment and settlement questions, insights, payment-link creation and supported refund actions, per[Razorpay’s launch announcement](https://razorpay.com/newsroom/razorpay-launches-a-conversational-ai-account-manager-ray-on-whatsapp-for-businesses-in-partnership-with-indusind-bank/) . The[Ray WhatsApp overview](https://razorpay.com/blog/meet-ray-your-always-on-ai-account-manager-now-live-on-whatsapp/) describes a security-verification link for authenticated account actions. Confirm rollout, access, permissions and available actions for your account. A status answer, a refund instruction and a final bank credit are separate events.


An illustrative scenario: a customer asks why a refund has not arrived. You retrieve the payment reference, confirm the refund was initiated and when, and tell the customer what has happened on your side. If the expected credit window has passed, you raise a Dashboard ticket with the payment ID and refund ID attached.


### Keep Dispute Evidence and Escalation Visible


The[disputes documentation](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/disputes/?preferred-country=IN) describes notifications, Dashboard review and evidence submission, including proof of delivery and invoices, with a respond-by deadline. The issuer decides the outcome of a contested dispute. That is a workflow benefit, not a guaranteed chargeback win.


Razorpay’s[published support process](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/dashboard/support/?preferred-country=IN) states that an escalation option becomes available on a ticket when its committed resolution TAT or SLA is not met, after which the case moves to a priority queue and a representative contacts you by phone within the next two hours. That is conditional contact, not a two-hour resolution promise. Live chat and callback are documented for selected users, with chat hours of 10 a.m. to 10 p.m. on working days.


### Compare AI Access and Controls Fairly


Payment Gateway A documents dashboard AI account assistance, a WhatsApp merchant assistant and separate AI operations agents. Payment Gateway B publishes 24/7 support and AI payment-page creation. Evaluate the tasks, permissions and escalation route each option makes available to your account. Ray gives eligible Razorpay merchants a conversational workflow to assess alongside the Dashboard support process. The standards body’s guidance on[securing AI in payment environments](https://blog.pcisecuritystandards.org/ai-principles-securing-the-use-of-ai-in-payment-environments) notes that where an AI has agency to perform actions, incident response planning must account for it.


**PRO-TIP #3:** Request the same demonstration from each provider: one account-specific payment query, one permitted refund action and one unresolved issue. Keep raw card details and API secrets out of chat.


## What Should You Check Before Launching or Changing Your Checkout?


Work through these seven steps and keep the output of each on file.


1. Record the legal entity, the payment activity and the selected integration.
2. Obtain current service-specific compliance evidence and record its scope and period.
3. Map the card-entry, order and payment-confirmation paths for your actual build.
4. Confirm your merchant validation requirement and which controls each party owns.
5. Test the permitted tokenisation, authentication and payment-status flows in the appropriate environment.
6. Check authorised access, logs, support attachments and the escalation route.
7. Approve launch through your own review process, and repeat after any material change.


Completing the checklist does not certify your business. It produces the records your reviewers, acquirer and auditors will ask for.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Does using Razorpay automatically make my business PCI DSS compliant?


No. A provider’s attestation covers its assessed entity and services. Your business still completes its own validation, usually a self-assessment questionnaire agreed with your acquirer, covering your website, scripts and processes. See our guide to[Razorpay Checkout and merchant PCI DSS responsibilities](https://razorpay.com/blog/pci-dss-compliant-payment-gateway-india/) .


### Are hosted fields, Standard Checkout and tokenisation the same thing?


No. Hosted fields isolate sensitive inputs inside provider-controlled components. Standard Checkout is a managed checkout experience. Tokenisation replaces a stored card credential with a reference for eligible later payments. Verify the exact integration you deploy.


### What is the difference between tokenisation and encryption in payment security?


Tokenisation replaces a payment credential with a substitute reference for an eligible payment flow. Encryption protects information using keys and can protect card data as well as names, addresses and order records. Card tokenisation does not automatically protect those other records, so apply appropriate encryption, access, retention and logging controls.


### What KYC and RBI evidence should I review before choosing a gateway?


Match the contracting legal entity and the payment activity against RBI’s published authorisation records, then review merchant KYC documents by business type, settlement terms and grievance routes. Start with our guide to[verifying an RBI-authorised payment aggregator](https://razorpay.com/blog/how-to-verify-an-rbi-authorised-payment-aggregator-in-india/) .


### Does Razorpay support 3DS2 for domestic and international cards?


Razorpay’s current[3DS2 documentation](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/payment-methods/cards/features/3ds2.0/?preferred-country=IN) describes support for international card payments, with browser and app channel differences. Confirm your domestic card authentication flow separately, since India’s requirements are set by RBI’s authentication directions.
